To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) reordering data to be loaded and (2) grouping load transactions on the same relation can significantly improve the performance of continuous data loading.
reordering and pre-aggregation can be used to reduce transaction deadlocks during continuous loading and improve performance.

(1) reordering the load transactions and grouping the data to be inserted can eliminate the deadlock problem in the presence of concurrent materialized join view load transactions; (2) pre-aggregation of data can significantly reduce the load time of materialized join view relations that contain aggregate attributes; and (3) reordering and grouping of load transactions can be used in combination with pre-aggregation to further reduce the load time for materialized join views with aggregate attributes
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problems.
how to load data into an RDBM in an efficient manner, and in particular how to load data continuously into an operational data warehouse.

the following issues in the context of operational data ware housing: (1) how to efficiently load data into the data warehouse, (2) how to load data in a way that is deadlock-free, and (3) how to reduce the load time of data warehouse transactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methods proposed in this thesis are useful and can be applied in a commercial RDBMS.

the proposed techniques are able to reduce the load time of a large data warehouse by a factor of 2 to 3, depending on the data size and the number of materialized join view base relations that are being updated simultaneously.
the proposed methods can significantly reduce the transaction overhead for continuous data loading, and thus improve the performance of operational data ware-housing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel method to reorder the data to be inserted into multiple relations in order to avoid deadlocks and improve load performance.
we have shown that the deadlock problem can be avoided by reordering the data loading, and that the number of SQL transactions can be significantly reduced by grouping the data loading.
we have developed a set of techniques for continuous data loading that can reduce the number of deadlocks, reduce the number of transactions in a load session and improve the load throughput.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for operational data warehousing applications, it is possible to load data into a materialized join view in a way that minimizes the number of SQL transactions and the time required for loading.
, by reordering the data and using pre-aggregation, it is possible to reduce the number and duration of the load transactions, thereby reducing the load time significantly.
